clue.text: Ex-directory union leader has STD line fixed

indicators.note: a leader is the front runner, so the first letter of union is taken
fixed in the sense of doctored or rigged, so the letters of STD and line are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: STD was the old British subscriber trunk dialling code
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trade union boss has had the long-distance phone line sorted, and the number is kept private.
explanation.walkthrough: U, the leader of union, is followed by NLISTED, which 'fixed' makes from STD and LINE. STD (subscriber trunk dialling) was the British term for direct long-distance dialling.
explanation.definitionFit: A number left out of the phone book is unlisted, the British phrase for that being ex-directory.

clue.text: Worried it could be difficult?

explanation.definitionFit: An uneasy person is anxious; read as un-easy, the word means not easy, so hard to do.

clue.text: Rarely tell doctor about it

indicators.note: about places the rearranged letters around the other piece
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of tell are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Seldom does anyone tell the doctor about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' rearranges TELL as L...TLE, which goes 'about' IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Little used as an adverb means hardly at all, as in little did they know.

clue.text: Fits new front wheel in fast

indicators.note: in puts the first letter of wheel inside the rearranged letters
new suggests making something over, so the letters of fits are rearranged
the front of wheel is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone fits a new front wheel to a bike in quick time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges FITS as S...IFT and W, the 'front' of wheel, goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift means quick, moving at speed.

clue.text: Round five to nine rising, say, for a time

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the piece for say encloses the rest

parts.note: EG, for example, is the short form for say
V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word nine is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something seems to happen at a time between five and nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'five to nine' looks like a clock time, but 'to' only joins five to the reversed nine; 'rising' turns nine upwards in this down entry, and 'Round' wraps the say piece about both.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening is a part of the day, the hours after the afternoon.

clue.text: Captain removing head of fish

indicators.note: taking away the head of the word drops its opening letter here

parts.note: a skipper is the captain of a ship or team

explanation.surface: A ship's captain cuts the head off a fish he has caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word: SKIPPER loses its first letter, S, and what is left is defined by 'fish'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kipper is a smoked herring, a fish eaten at breakfast in Britain.

clue.text: Strangely it is more about having equal dimensions

indicators.note: strangely means oddly, so the letters of it, is and more are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Something oddly turns out to be bigger, with equal measurements throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges IT IS MORE as ISOMETRI, and C, short for circa ('about'), comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometric describes figures whose dimensions are of the same measure, as in an isometric cube drawing.

clue.text: Prayer (small one before performing)

parts.note: petit is French for small, also used in English as in petit four
I is the Roman numeral for one
a performer is on when on stage

explanation.surface: A child's little prayer said before going on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads like a stage direction for a child; 'before' just sets the small and one pieces ahead of the performing one.
explanation.definitionFit: A petition is a request, especially a solemn plea to God.

clue.text: Engineers likely to be dependable

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army's engineering corps
liable means likely, as in liable to happen

explanation.surface: Engineers are thought likely to be trustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliable means trustworthy, able to be counted on.

clue.text: Required to follow poor Eden around

indicators.note: around tells us the rearranged Eden goes on the outside, wrapping the other piece
poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters of Eden are rearranged

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: Someone was obliged to trail behind the unfortunate Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: Eden may suggest Anthony Eden, the British prime minister; 'poor' splits his name around the following piece, which 'around' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Entailed means necessitated, so a thing entailed is one that was needed or demanded.

clue.text: Those turning Left finding somewhere to stay

indicators.note: turning the word around in all directions rearranges the letters of those

explanation.surface: Travellers who turn left at the junction come upon a place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those turning Left' reads like drivers at a junction; 'turning' is the anagram signal and 'finding' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostel is cheap lodging, a place where travellers stay the night.

clue.text: Exhausted Asian in club

indicators.note: in places the letter for Asian inside the word for club

parts.note: a bat is a club used to hit a ball
E stands for Eastern, so Asian here

explanation.surface: A tired-out Asian member of a social club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a society but is the bat; E (Eastern) goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat means worn out, as in dead beat.

clue.text: Diamond I stole is around — look inside

indicators.note: inside places the second piece within the rearranged letters
around here means moved about, so the letters of I and stole are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
an air is a look or manner, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: A jewel thief confesses to stealing a diamond and invites someone to look inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reads as a place but rearranges I stole; 'inside' then sets the look piece within it, and 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitaire is a single diamond set on its own, as in a ring.

clue.text: Unusually cunning, kiss sweetheart back!

indicators.note: back tells us the whole run of pieces is read from its end to its start

parts.note: art can mean cunning or craftiness
X is the cross used for a kiss at the end of a letter
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging a lover to be extra clever and kiss back.
explanation.walkthrough: ART, X and E read 'back' together give E, X, TRA. 'Unusually' works as the definition through phrases like 'extra careful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra used as an adverb means more than usually, as in extra large.

clue.text: Pine from end to end

explanation.definitionFit: To pine is to yearn or crave; a line running from end to end runs lengthwise, the full length of something.

clue.text: Not bothered, laughs uncontrollably during attack

indicators.note: during means within, so the second rearrangement sits inside the first
bothered means flustered, so the letters of not are mixed up
uncontrollably means wildly, so the letters of laughs are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone unfazed laughs helplessly while under assault.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagram signals work separately: 'bothered' on Not and 'uncontrollably' on laughs, and 'during' sets the second within the first.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce attack or assault.

clue.text: Our Tim, turned. 50, causes an uproar

indicators.note: turned means flipped about, so the letters of our and Tim are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Our Tim has just reached fifty and is creating a commotion about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' looks like a birthday age but is the anagram signal; 'causes an' joins wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great disturbance and confusion, a commotion.

clue.text: Sam's not prepared to take note. Jock

indicators.note: to take means to hold within, so the letter for note goes inside
prepared means made ready or arranged, so the letters of Sam's and not are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S, taken as written
taken as written
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: Sam is not ready to take notes from a Scottish man.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is British slang for a man from Scotland. 'prepared' is the anagram signal, and the S of Sam's counts here.
explanation.definitionFit: Jock is a slang word for a man from Scotland.

clue.text: Joined doctor inside once Id changed

indicators.note: inside places the doctor's letters within the rearranged letters
changed means altered, so the letters of once and Id are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist joined the session once the patient's id had altered.
explanation.walkthrough: The id is the instinctive part of the mind in Freud's theory, which makes the surface sound psychiatric; 'changed' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Combined means joined together or united.

clue.text: Angry little man when thwarted

parts.note: cross means annoyed or angry
Ed is a short form of the man's name Edward

explanation.surface: A small man gets annoyed whenever someone gets in his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link word between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossed means opposed or frustrated, as in crossed in love.

clue.text: What's owed on cot (upright model)

indicators.note: upright in a down clue means the word is set going up, so read in reverse

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
the Model T was the famous early Ford car

explanation.surface: A note of the money owed for a cot and an upright display model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upright' looks like describing a model; in a down entry it means written bottom to top. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is a sum of money due to someone.

clue.text: Very short distance from home to church

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Someone who lives right next to the church has hardly any distance to walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'to' tie the two pieces to the definition, IN first then CH.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a tiny unit of length, used for any very small distance.

clue.text: French king races round after fashionable anthem

indicators.note: after puts this piece behind the word for fashionable

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing

indicators.note: round means the race letters surround the king

parts.note: the TT races are the motorcycle Tourist Trophy races on the Isle of Man
roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A French monarch hurries round after a stylish piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race, so 'races' gives two Ts that go 'round' the French king, all 'after' fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: An introit is a psalm or anthem sung at the start of a church service.

clue.text: "What half?' poor Enid moaned

indicators.note: half means the first two of the four letters of what
poor means in sorry shape, so the letters of Enid are rearranged

explanation.surface: Poor Enid grumbled at being asked which half.
explanation.walkthrough: WH is 'half' of What and 'poor' rearranges ENID as INED.
explanation.definitionFit: Whined means complained in a high, plaintive voice.

clue.text: Rotten theologian in crooked deal

indicators.note: in puts the theologian's letters inside the rearranged letters
crooked means bent, so the letters of deal are rearranged

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A churchman caught up in a dishonest bargain is corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges DEAL as A...LED, with DD 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: An addled egg is a rotten one.

clue.text: Jack's taking it back — I swallowed a bone

indicators.note: the letter I is swallowed, taken inside the other letters
back means the joined pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB, able seaman, is a sailor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Jack takes something back while another person admits to swallowing a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a sailor, here an able seaman; 'back' turns the sailor and it together, and 'swallowed' takes the I in. 'taking' and 'a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger of the two bones in the lower leg.

clue.text: Fiance could be hotter in bed!

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word bed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of hotter can be made into something else

explanation.surface: Someone muses that their intended might be steamier between the sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges HOTTER as ETROTH, which goes 'in' B...ED. The noun means a person engaged to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: One's betrothed is the person one is engaged to marry, an intended spouse.

clue.text: Board requiring consent of two Europeans

parts.note: oui is French for yes
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A committee whose work needs the agreement of two Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a committee; it is the board used at seances. 'requiring' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is a lettered board used in seances to spell out messages from spirits.

clue.text: Servant with years to run

parts.note: a man is a manservant, a male servant
an age is a long span of years

explanation.surface: A servant who has years left in him before retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins MAN and AGE, and 'to' links them to the definition 'run'.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage a business is to run it, being in charge of it.

clue.text: Ideal loo at inn needs renovating

indicators.note: renovating means rebuilding, so the letters of loo, at and inn are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The toilet at the pub is badly in need of a refit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs renovating' rearranges LOO AT INN. 'Ideal' is the adjective meaning existing only in the mind, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Notional and ideal both describe something that exists only as an idea, imagined rather than real.

clue.text: Terribly untidy naturists go for it

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters of untidy are rearranged

explanation.surface: Messy nudists just let it all hang out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges UNTIDY. The definition is a description: naturists are people who go without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists favour being without clothes, which is nakedness.

clue.text: Good man darned mad if left without transport

parts.note: ST, for saint, is the crossword stand-in for a good man

indicators.note: mad means crazy or wild, so the letters of darned are rearranged

explanation.surface: A decent fellow would be furious if he were left with no way to get home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'darned mad' reads like mild swearing; 'mad' is the anagram signal on darned, and 'if' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stranded is to be stuck somewhere with no means of getting away.
